title: When does rotor cant pay on a small quadrotor co-designed with its motors and controller?
lede: research programme: fixed rotor cant on a co-designed quadrotor; cant cuts held-out attitude error by 4.2° under INDI, 4.9° under geometric SO(3) control and 5.3° under PID (10 of 10 seeds each), so it is not a patch for a weak controller; the co-designed cant stays near 34° under all three laws and under a price on hover power
summary: An open research programme (target IEEE RA-L) on when a fixed rotor cant angle pays on a small quadrotor once arm, propeller, motor headroom and attitude controller are designed with it. Milestone 1 found that the torque limits of seven earlier simulated steps understated yaw authority by 2× to 2.8×; cant still beat no cant by 4.8° RMS. Milestone 2 makes roll, pitch and yaw share one thrust polytope through an attitude-priority mixer (as PX4 and Betaflight do) and puts a price on hover power. Without cant the tuned vehicle saturates roll and pitch on 97% of steps and yaw gets nothing; cant's paired advantage grows to 6.08° (SD 0.28, 5 of 5 seeds). Pricing power at 0.3° per 100 W cuts hover power 4–7× for under 0.5° of error, but the chosen cant stays at 28–37° in 9 of 10 seed-arms (best of three CMA-ES starts), refuting the hypothesis of a small 5–20° optimum; cant still wins the priced objective in 5 of 5 seeds at 0.3 and 4 of 5 at 1° per 100 W. Single-start CMA-ES is unreliable on the polytope (2 of 5 seeds fell to low cant). Milestone 4 asks whether cant only patches a weak controller: with incremental nonlinear dynamic inversion (INDI) or geometric SO(3) attitude control co-designed in place of PID (10 seeds, three CMA-ES starts each), cant still wins by 4.18° (INDI), 4.88° (geometric) and 5.27° (PID) in 10 of 10 seeds, and INDI without cant is 4.02° worse than PID with cant in 10 of 10. INDI narrows the gap by 1.1° and mostly steadies the uncanted vehicle; the chosen cant stays at a 34–35° median under every law. Simulated; TWR fixed at 2; the power price is a swept modelling choice; mass, cost and motor fits and plant ranges are inherited assumptions; no hardware.
